answer: A comet may sign one admission echo in its life, and only for a head whose payment lineage it does not share — clones cannot sponsor clones. Signing spends the echo forever and locks the comet's jade behind that head for its whole life; the ledger prices each lock at base times one plus the fakes already unmasked in the newcomer's lineage. An operator's k-th identity therefore needs the k-th distinct outside comet's only echo plus a lock of base×(1+j) once j of its fakes are unmasked — every scandal steepens its own curve — while a fresh comet's sponsor locks plain base.
